categories.main_business_segments: CDW operates three reportable segments: Corporate (serving US private sector businesses with more than 250 employees), Small Business (serving US private sector businesses with up to 250 employees), and Public (serving US government agencies, education, and healthcare institutions). Additionally, CDW UK and CDW Canada are included in an 'Other' category as they do not meet the quantitative thresholds for reportable segments.
categories.core_technologies_production_methods: CDW provides a broad array of IT solutions, including hardware (notebooks, desktops, servers, networking, collaboration, storage), software (cloud, security, productivity, virtualization), and services (advisory, design, implementation, managed services). Solutions are delivered across on-premise, hybrid, and cloud environments, leveraging integration, configuration, and logistics capabilities, and supported by partnerships with over 1,000 vendor partners.
categories.primary_customers_markets: CDW serves over 250,000 customers across business, government, education, and healthcare sectors in the US, UK, and Canada. Key customer types include large enterprises, small and medium businesses, federal/state/local government agencies, K-12 and higher education institutions, and healthcare providers.
categories.geographic_coverage: CDW's primary markets are the United States (about 90% of net sales), the United Kingdom, and Canada, with capabilities to provide integrated IT solutions in approximately 150 countries for customers with primary locations in these regions.
categories.supply_chain_position: CDW operates as a value-added reseller and solutions integrator in the midstream of the IT supply chain, procuring products from OEMs, software publishers, cloud providers, and wholesale distributors, and delivering integrated solutions and services to end customers.
categories.strategic_focus_rd_direction: CDW's strategic priorities include expanding its integrated solutions and services portfolio, investing in digital transformation, cloud, security, and artificial intelligence capabilities, and enhancing its technical expertise and customer engagement. The company is also focused on system transformation initiatives, including a new ERP implementation, and on developing talent and innovation excellence.
categories.revenue_model: CDW generates revenue primarily through the sale of hardware, software, and services, acting as both principal and agent depending on the offering. Revenue streams include product sales (hardware/software), professional and managed services, cloud and SaaS subscriptions, and value-added integration and logistics services.
categories.key_competitors_industry_positioning: CDW faces competition from IT resellers, direct-selling manufacturers, large service providers, system integrators, cloud providers, e-commerce companies, and office supply retailers. Key peers include Accenture, Arrow Electronics, Avnet, Insight Enterprises, TD SYNNEX, and Best Buy, among others. CDW is positioned as a leading multi-brand IT solutions provider with significant scale and end-market diversity.
categories.financial_scale_growth_profile: In 2024, CDW reported net sales of $21.0 billion, gross profit of $4.6 billion, and net income of $1.08 billion. The company experienced a 1.8% year-over-year decline in net sales, reflecting cautious customer IT spending amid economic uncertainty, but maintained strong gross profit margins and operating income. CDW is a Fortune 500 and S&P 500 company with a history of profitable growth and significant cash flow generation.
categories.value_proposition_product_differentiatio: CDW differentiates itself through its broad multi-brand IT solutions portfolio, deep technical expertise, and ability to simplify complex technology decisions for customers. The company provides unique value by acting as a trusted advisor, offering tailored solutions across the IT lifecycle, and leveraging strong vendor relationships to deliver competitive pricing, integration, and implementation capabilities.
